08. End-to-End Nested Survival Run and Multi-Machine Sharding on Rossi Data

Source: vignettes/rossi_nested_survival.Rmd
rossi_nested_survival.Rmd

Overview

In multi-domain clinical survival pipelines, each domain report traditionally strings together ~150 lines of boilerplate:

  1. Validate counting-process intervals (validate_start_stop())
  2. Construct subject-grouped nested folds (rsample::nested_cv() + rsample::group_vfold_cv())
  3. Inner hyperparameter tuning (tune_alpha_by_split())
  4. Candidate model selection (select_candidate_models())
  5. Outer-fold scoring (score_outer())
  6. Predictor importance & selection stability (summarize_outer_importance())
  7. Censoring weight sensitivity comparison (compare_censoring_weights())

This vignette demonstrates how to run the entire nested survival workflow on the packaged rossi_data() recidivism cohort:

  • One-call execution with nested_survival_run() (including summary(), plot(), and tidy() methods)
  • Sharding across machines with shard = c(1, 2) and shard = c(2, 2), merging completed shards with collect_checkpoints(), and pruning stale checkpoints with clean_checkpoints()
  • Self-rendering reproducibility appendix via repro_appendix() 
library(TempleCBE)
library(recipes)
library(rsample)
library(survival)
library(dplyr)

1. Preparing rossi_data() in Start/Stop Format

The packaged rossi_data() dataset tracks 432 individuals over a 52-week follow-up window with baseline covariates (fin, age, race, wexp, mar, paro, prio, educ) and weekly employment indicators (emp1–emp52).

For a fast, self-contained demonstration, we convert a 90-subject subset of rossi_data() into counting-process (tstart, tstop, status) intervals and run validate_start_stop() to verify interval integrity and censoring rate:

raw_rossi <- rossi_data()

# Construct counting-process (tstart, tstop, status) intervals per subject
rossi_cohort <- raw_rossi |>
  slice(1:90) |>
  mutate(
    id = row_number(),
    tstart = 0,
    tstop = as.numeric(week),
    status = as.integer(arrest)
  ) |>
  select(id, tstart, tstop, status, fin, age, race, wexp, mar, paro, prio, educ)

val <- validate_start_stop(
  rossi_cohort,
  id = "id",
  start = "tstart",
  stop = "tstop",
  status = "status"
)
val
#> TempleCBE Start/Stop Survival Data Check
#> ----------------------------------------
#> Subjects:               90 (21 with event, 69 censored [76.7%])
#> Intervals (rows):       90 (events: 21, missing: 0)
#> Overlapping intervals:  0
#> Gapped intervals:       0
#> Events before last row: 0
#> Rows after an event:    0
#> Non-positive intervals: 0
#> Tied times:             72 stop time(s), 3 event time(s)
#> Status:                 VALID

2. One-Call Nested Survival Run (nested_survival_run())

nested_survival_run() executes all seven stages in order, writes fingerprinted checkpoints and render_manifest.json into run_dir, and resumes automatically if rerun with identical data and settings:

run_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "rossi_e1_run")

rec <- recipe(~ ., data = rossi_cohort) |>
  update_role(id, tstart, tstop, status, new_role = "id variable")

features <- c("fin", "age", "race", "wexp", "mar", "paro", "prio", "educ")
candidate_formulas <- c(
  "fin + age + prio",
  "fin + age + race + wexp + mar + paro + prio + educ"
)

rossi_run <- nested_survival_run(
  data = rossi_cohort,
  recipe = rec,
  id = "id",
  start = "tstart",
  stop = "tstop",
  status = "status",
  domain = "Recidivism",
  run_dir = run_dir,
  feature_names = features,
  formulas = candidate_formulas,
  outer_v = 3,
  inner_v = 3,
  alphas = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8),
  top_n = 2,
  internal_folds = 3,
  cox.ties = "breslow",
  seed = 67025
)

rossi_run
#> <cbe_nested_survival_run> Domain: Recidivism [completed]
#>   Subjects: 90 (Events: 21, Censored: 69 [76.7%])
#>   Outer folds: 3 | Candidate models: 4 | Outer fits: 12
#>   Median outer IBS: 0.0714 (IQR: 0.0521) | Seed: 67025 (v0.5.6)
#>   Run directory: /tmp/RtmpptqoTk/rossi_e1_run (fingerprint: 57dc98da715b)

3. Sharding Across Machines and Merging with collect_checkpoints()

When a tuning or outer-scoring grid spans multiple outer folds and domains, work can be split across n machines sharing a network drive (or synced checkpoint directory) using shard = c(i, n):

  • Machine 1 runs shard = c(1, 2)
  • Machine 2 runs shard = c(2, 2)
  • Once all shards finish, collect_checkpoints() verifies that every checkpoint file shares the same checkpoint_run_fingerprint and seed_scheme ("v0.5.6") and binds them into a single table identical to a single-machine run.

Step-by-Step Sharded Tuning & Outer Scoring 

shard_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "rossi_sharded_checkpoints")
tune_ckpt_dir <- file.path(shard_dir, "tune_fold1")
score_ckpt_dir <- file.path(shard_dir, "score_outer")

# the fold assignment is random: without a seed a build occasionally drew a fold without events
set.seed(67025)
nested_splits <- nested_cv(
  rossi_cohort,
  outside = group_vfold_cv(group = id, v = 2),
  inside = group_vfold_cv(group = id, v = 2)
)
times_df <- unique(rossi_cohort[, c("tstart", "tstop")])

# --- Machine 1 evaluates Shard 1 of 2 ---
tune_shard_1 <- tune_alpha_by_split(
  object = nested_splits$inner_resamples[[1]],
  recipe = rec,
  feature_names = features,
  alphas = c(0.25, 0.75),
  time_data = times_df,
  internal_folds = 3,
  cox.ties = "breslow",
  checkpoint_dir = tune_ckpt_dir,
  shard = c(1, 2),
  seed = 67025
)

# --- Machine 2 evaluates Shard 2 of 2 ---
tune_shard_2 <- tune_alpha_by_split(
  object = nested_splits$inner_resamples[[1]],
  recipe = rec,
  feature_names = features,
  alphas = c(0.25, 0.75),
  time_data = times_df,
  internal_folds = 3,
  cox.ties = "breslow",
  checkpoint_dir = tune_ckpt_dir,
  shard = c(2, 2),
  seed = 67025
)

# --- Merge shards with collect_checkpoints() ---
merged_tune <- collect_checkpoints(tune_ckpt_dir, type = "tune")
merged_tune
#> # A tibble: 32 × 6
#>    inner_resamples_splits    IBS lambda term  estimate alpha
#>    <chr>                   <dbl>  <dbl> <chr>    <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1 1                      0.0803  0.753 fin          0  0.25
#>  2 1                      0.0803  0.753 age          0  0.25
#>  3 1                      0.0803  0.753 race         0  0.25
#>  4 1                      0.0803  0.753 wexp         0  0.25
#>  5 1                      0.0803  0.753 mar          0  0.25
#>  6 1                      0.0803  0.753 paro         0  0.25
#>  7 1                      0.0803  0.753 prio         0  0.25
#>  8 1                      0.0803  0.753 educ         0  0.25
#>  9 1                      0.0803  0.251 fin          0  0.75
#> 10 1                      0.0803  0.251 age          0  0.75
#> # ℹ 22 more rows

# Select candidate models from merged tuning results
cand_grid <- select_candidate_models(
  merged_tune,
  formulas = candidate_formulas,
  top_n = 2
)
cand_grid
#> # A tibble: 4 × 3
#>   model                                                          alpha formula  
#>   <chr>                                                          <dbl> <chr>    
#> 1 alpha=0.25; fin + age + prio                                    0.25 fin + ag…
#> 2 alpha=0.75; fin + age + prio                                    0.75 fin + ag…
#> 3 alpha=0.25; fin + age + race + wexp + mar + paro + prio + educ  0.25 fin + ag…
#> 4 alpha=0.75; fin + age + race + wexp + mar + paro + prio + educ  0.75 fin + ag…

Now we shard outer-fold evaluation (score_outer()) across two machines and merge the results:

# Machine 1: Shard 1 of 2
score_outer(
  object = nested_splits,
  grid = cand_grid,
  recipe = rec,
  feature_names = features,
  time_data = times_df,
  internal_folds = 3,
  cox.ties = "breslow",
  checkpoint_dir = score_ckpt_dir,
  shard = c(1, 2),
  seed = 67025
)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 7
#>   outer_fold model                      alpha formula    IBS lambda coefficients
#>   <chr>      <chr>                      <dbl> <chr>    <dbl>  <dbl> <list>      
#> 1 Resample1  alpha=0.25; fin + age + p…  0.25 fin + … 0.0850 0.0188 <tibble>    
#> 2 Resample1  alpha=0.25; fin + age + r…  0.25 fin + … 0.0841 0.132  <tibble>    
#> 3 Resample2  alpha=0.25; fin + age + p…  0.25 fin + … 0.0960 0.510  <tibble>    
#> 4 Resample2  alpha=0.25; fin + age + r…  0.25 fin + … 0.0960 0.510  <tibble>

# Machine 2: Shard 2 of 2
score_outer(
  object = nested_splits,
  grid = cand_grid,
  recipe = rec,
  feature_names = features,
  time_data = times_df,
  internal_folds = 3,
  cox.ties = "breslow",
  checkpoint_dir = score_ckpt_dir,
  shard = c(2, 2),
  seed = 67025
)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 7
#>   outer_fold model                     alpha formula    IBS  lambda coefficients
#>   <chr>      <chr>                     <dbl> <chr>    <dbl>   <dbl> <list>

#> 4 Resample2  alpha=0.75; fin + age + …  0.75 fin + … 0.0960 0.170   <tibble>

# Merge outer-fold checkpoints
merged_outer <- collect_checkpoints(score_ckpt_dir, type = "score_outer")
merged_outer

# Summarize predictor importance across outer folds

Cleaning Up Old Checkpoints (clean_checkpoints())

If inputs or settings change in a subsequent run, clean_checkpoints(dir, keep = "current") inspects all checkpoint .rds files and removes superseded or mismatched files while preserving the active run’s checkpoints:

clean_checkpoints(score_ckpt_dir, keep = "current", dry_run = TRUE)
#> TempleCBE Checkpoint Cleanup
#> ----------------------------
#> Kept:    8 file(s)
#> Removed: 0 file(s) (dry run)

4. Self-Rendering Reproducibility Appendix (repro_appendix())

Every report can end with repro_appendix(), which records package versions, git commit, RNG seed, seed_scheme, active future::plan(), dataset SHA-256 hashes, validate_start_stop() results, checkpoint fingerprints, and the render manifest:

repro_appendix(run = rossi_run, heading_level = 3)
